question.problem: Find the measure of the side $\overset{―}{AB}$ of the triangle $△ABC$ if $AC=3.1$, $BC=0.7,$ and the measure of $\overset{―}{AB}$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the measure of $\overset{―}{AB}.$

According to the triangle inequality theorem, the length of any side must be

- greater than the difference between the lengths of the other two sides, and

- less than the sum of those lengths.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Difference} & <x<\text{Sum} \\ 3.1-0.7 & <x<3.1+0.7 \\ 2.4 & <x<3.8.\end{aligned}
$$

The only integer satisfying this condition is $3.$
